title: Medivault - Security review: data residency & region pinning
summary: Medivault (healthcare SaaS) did a security/compliance deep-dive with Redwood AE+SE focused on data residency and region pinning needs for US/EU data, cross-border processing concerns, sub-processor disclosures, and encryption/KMS. Discussed Redwood's region pinning options, private VPC deployment, key management options (bring-your-own-key vs Redwood KMS), audit logs, and SSO/RBAC integration. Action items: send SOC 2 + ISO docs, provide diagram of region routing and sub-processor list, share KMS integration guide and pilot test plan.
next_steps: Maya to share SOC2 report, ISO summary, and sub-processor list (by 2026-12-03)
Diego to prepare KMS BYOK integration notes and sample config (by 2026-12-06)
Schedule a technical pilot (region-pinned Dedicated env) with Tom after docs are reviewed (target week of 2026-12-13)
Medivault to confirm regulatory requirements for EU-only processing and legal to review sub-processor agreements
action_items: Maya Chen - Send SOC2 Type II report + ISO summary + sub-processor list - due 2026-12-03
Diego Alvarez - Provide KMS BYOK guide, sample config, and network diagram for VPC private deployment - due 2026-12-06
Tom Reynolds (Medivault) - Share list of datasets and EU-only flows for pilot scoping - due 2026-12-08
Aisha Khan (Medivault Legal) - Review sub-processor DPA clauses and follow up with Redwood legal - due 2026-12-10
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick intro — I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. with me is Diego, our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Sara Patel: Hi Maya, hi Diego, Sara here. I'm the CISO at Medivault. we want to focus on residency and region pinning — EU patient records, no cross border.
[00:21] Tom Reynolds: Tom, cloud architect. we'll talk ops and networking.
[00:25] Aisha Khan: Aisha from legal — i'll focus on sub-processor and DPA stuff.
[00:30] Diego Alvarez: thanks team. agenda: quick security overview, region pinning options (hosted vs dedicated vs private), KMS options, audit logs, sub-processors, then Q&A.
[00:45] Maya Chen: just to set expectations, we'll try to cover both compliance posture and technical patterns; if we need follow-ups we'll do a technical pilot.
[01:15] Sara Patel: our primary reqs: EU-only processing for PHI, no tokens leaving EU, and proof that backup/replica data is also EU. can Redwood guarantee that?
[01:30] Diego Alvarez: short answer: yes, with region pinning + private deployment options. hosted API can be region-scoped for most customers but for strict EU-only we recommend Dedicated or Private (VPC) where routing and egress are controlled.
[01:50] Tom Reynolds: can you explain differences? like if we use hosted in eu-west, are there sub-processors in the US who might process metadata?
[02:05] Maya Chen: great question; we do have a list of sub-processors — storage, monitoring, logging — most are regional, but some analytics and ops services have US-based components. we'll share the full sub-processor list. for EU-only PHI we usually suggest Dedicated in EU or Private on-prem/VPC.
[02:30] Aisha Khan: legal wants to see contractual guarantees and technical proofs — do you support contractual region commitments in the DPA?
[02:45] Maya Chen: yes, we have DPA language and addenda for data residency restrictions; exceptions are detailed in sub-processor appendices. we'll send current DPA samples.
[03:10] Diego Alvarez: on the technical side, region pinning options: 1) hosted region pinning — route requests to EU cluster; 2) Dedicated reserved capacity in EU — isolated GPU pools; 3) Private deployment — control plane in customer VPC or on-premises for air-gapped.
[03:35] Sara Patel: for backups and async processing, how do you ensure they remain in EU? snapshots, logs, etc?
[03:50] Diego Alvarez: snapshots and backups can be configured to stay in-region for Dedicated/Private. for hosted we can provide policy-level guarantees but some telemetry might cross borders for ops; that's why we recommend Dedicated/Private for strict requirements.
[04:15] Tom Reynolds: what about KMS? we need BYOK (bring-your-own-key) and HSM support.
[04:28] Diego Alvarez: we support both Redwood-managed KMS and BYOK via customer KMS (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS). HSM integrations are possible for Private deployments; for hosted we offer envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in many regions.
[04:50] Sara Patel: important: keys must never be exported. can you confirm lifecycle and key rotation policies?
[05:00] Maya Chen: yes, keys under BYOK remain in customer's KMS; Redwood stores only key references (not raw key material). rotation is supported; we'll provide the exact rotation procedures and requirements.
[05:25] Aisha Khan: any third-party access to raw data for debugging or support?
[05:35] Diego Alvarez: access policies: for Dedicated and Private, access is restricted; for hosted, support access is controlled via IAM, and we use just-in-time escalation with audit logs. we can also provide options to disable remote debug access.
[06:00] Sara Patel: audit logs — are they immutable, do they contain request/response tokens or just metadata?
[06:15] Diego Alvarez: audit logs include metadata, request IDs, timestamps, and user IDs. we do not log full request content by default for PHI customers; there are settings to redact or truncate. logs can be exported to customer-owned logging endpoints in EU.
[06:40] Tom Reynolds: latency impact if we pin to EU Dedicated vs hosted multi-region?
[06:50] Diego Alvarez: Dedicated in-region gives consistent latency; multi-region hosted may route to nearest healthy region but could cause cross-border in edge cases. we'll share performance profiles from our catalog for EU models.
[07:15] Sara Patel: sub-processors — we need the full list and data flow diagram, especially any US-based vendors.
[07:25] Maya Chen: we'll share a current sub-processor list and a redlineable DPA. note that some infra vendors (monitoring, observability) have US components; we can detail what data they see.
[07:45] Aisha Khan: how do you handle legal process requests (e.g., US warrants) if data resides in EU?
[07:55] Diego Alvarez: jurisdiction follows data residency and contractual commitments; for Private and Dedicated located in EU we push back and route legal requests to the customer or follow the DPA process. we'll involve legal for specifics.
[08:20] Tom Reynolds: from networking perspective, for VPC option do you support private endpoints, direct connect, or peering?
[08:30] Diego Alvarez: yes, we support private endpoints, AWS Direct Connect/ExpressRoute equivalents, and peering for Private deployments; Dedicated can also be configured with private networking. we'll provide a diagram.
[09:00] Sara Patel: encryption at rest and in transit specifics? TLS versions, cipher suites?
[09:12] Diego Alvarez: TLS 1.2+ supported, default TLS 1.3 for all inter-service and client-server traffic; at-rest encryption uses AES-256. we'll include crypto/algorithm appendix in the docs.
[09:40] Maya Chen: quick interjection — customers often ask about cross-border analytics. Diego, can you explain how metadata flows might leave region and mitigation?
[09:52] Diego Alvarez: sure: telemetry and metrics are often aggregated in central analytics; for strict regimes we can route telemetry to EU-only analytics or disable telemetry export. we also provide sampling and redaction.
[10:15] Sara Patel: do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001? we need proof.
[10:22] Maya Chen: yes, SOC 2 Type II available; ISO 27001 in progress or a summary? (slight pause) we have ISO 27001 certified for core infra as of last quarter — we'll attach certs.
[10:40] Aisha Khan: can we get a pen test summary and recent remediation notes?
[10:45] Maya Chen: absolutely, we'll share the high-level pentest report and remediation timeline redacted as needed.
[11:05] Tom Reynolds: about backups — retention policies: can we control retention and enforce EU-only retention?
[11:15] Diego Alvarez: retention configurable in Dedicated/Private; for hosted there's a retention policy with additives for enterprise customers. snapshots can be restricted to EU buckets.
[11:40] Sara Patel: curious about model caching and KV cache — any chance cached tokens could traverse regions?
[11:50] Diego Alvarez: our KV cache is per-region for Dedicated/Private; for hosted there are global caches for efficiency but you can opt out. for PHI we recommend region-isolated caches.
[12:10] Maya Chen: moving on — can you outline a pilot plan if Medivault wants to validate EU-only processing?
[12:20] Tom Reynolds: yes, we'd do test dataset flows, real request tracing, and audit log verification. also latency and failover tests.
[12:30] Diego Alvarez: pilot suggestion: 1) spin up a Dedicated EU environment, 2) configure customer KMS BYOK, 3) run sample population with redaction, 4) review audit logs exported to customer logging in EU, 5) run fault injection. we'll draft a runbook.
[12:55] Sara Patel: what about data subject requests and deletion? if a patient requests deletion, how do you ensure model caches or backups are deleted?
[13:05] Diego Alvarez: we have deletion flows; for Dedicated/Private we can scrub KV caches and remove snapshots on request. for hosted we have data deletion APIs and retention enforcement — we'll share exact SLA for deletion.
[13:35] Aisha Khan: concerning sub-processors again — please confirm notification windows for adding new sub-processors.
[13:45] Maya Chen: contractual notification windows are typically 30-60 days for major sub-processor changes; specifics in DPA.
[14:05] Tom Reynolds: network egress logging — can we get per-flow egress logs for auditing?
[14:15] Diego Alvarez: yes, we can furnish egress logs, VPC flow logs, and they can be exported to your EU logging endpoint.
[14:40] Sara Patel: any limitations on model weights or open model variants in EU vs US?
[14:50] Diego Alvarez: model availability varies by region; most open models are available EU-side but there are licensing and GPU availability constraints. we'll provide the catalog for EU models and throughput targets.
[15:10] Maya Chen: quick micro-ask — what are your timelines and decision blockers to run a pilot?
[15:20] Tom Reynolds: decision is contingent on legal sign-off and receiving SOC2, sub-processor list, and KMS integration guide. timing depends on legal turnaround but target to start mid-December.
[15:40] Sara Patel: do you have any references of healthcare customers using region-pinning?
[15:48] Maya Chen: yes, we have a couple of redacted case studies; we'll share references after NDA if needed.
[16:05] Diego Alvarez: also note that for ultra-sensitive workloads we recommend Private with on-prem control plane and HSM — gives max control.
[16:30] Aisha Khan: from legal side, can you accept EU data residency as a contractual obligation with defined penalties?
[16:40] Maya Chen: we can discuss tailored addenda; depends on the engagement (Dedicated/Private) and procurement. we'll have legal follow up.
[17:00] Tom Reynolds: operational question: how are backups encrypted with BYOK? are snapshots encrypted using customer key?
[17:10] Diego Alvarez: yes, snapshots for BYOK are encrypted under customer-managed keys when configured; we'll share config examples.
[17:35] Sara Patel: compliance automation — any hooks for automated evidence collection for audits?
[17:45] Maya Chen: Redwood Console has audit exports, compliance evidence bundles, and we can schedule periodic evidence pulls. we'll include sample reports.
[18:05] Diego Alvarez: small caveat: some telemetry used for runtime optimization is aggregated; for strict customers we can disable aggregation or route through EU-only telemetry collectors.
[18:30] Tom Reynolds: what about cross-border subcontractors — do you use any US-based devops teams that might access logs?
[18:45] Maya Chen: we have global ops teams but access controls are strict; for Dedicated/Private you can restrict support access entirely and require VPN/JIT. we'll provide an access matrix.
[19:10] Aisha Khan: software supply chain — do you publish SBOMs for runtime components?
[19:20] Diego Alvarez: yes, we can provide SBOMs and dependency lists as part of security package.
[19:40] Sara Patel: incident response — SLAs and notification timelines?
[19:50] Maya Chen: incident classification and notif windows: P1 immediate notif, full report within 72 hours, remediation timeline depending on severity. enterprise SLA can tighten that.
[20:10] Tom Reynolds: cross-border processing exceptions — if there's a transient failover to US region, how is data handled?
[20:20] Diego Alvarez: we have fallback policies: can be set to fail closed (reject) or fail open (route to next region). for EU-only we set fail-closed and alert.
[20:45] Sara Patel: can you produce a proof-of-routing — a trace showing requests stay in EU?
[20:55] Diego Alvarez: yes, we can provide request traces and signed attestations for pilot runs.
[21:20] Maya Chen: let's talk about the DPA and sub-processor list logistics — Diego will circulate docs, legal will be copied.
[21:30] Aisha Khan: we will need redlines and time to review. also please canvas any data residency exceptions in the DPA.
[21:50] Diego Alvarez: technical note on KMS: for AWS KMS BYOK we support key policies that prevent key usage outside eu-west region; customer needs to configure the key grants — we'll include step-by-step.
[22:20] Tom Reynolds: what about e-discovery and law enforcement? if data is in EU, we want Redwood to route requests to our legal team not disclose.
[22:35] Maya Chen: that's standard — we'll escalate such requests through the DPA process; legal will coordinate.
[23:00] Sara Patel: performance testing — can you run a small benchmark in a dedicated EU pool?
[23:10] Diego Alvarez: absolutely, we can provision a small Dedicated pool for a short benchmark; we'll include test harness and token-level cost estimate.
[23:40] Aisha Khan: any further encryption-at-rest caveats for backups stored in object storage?
[23:50] Diego Alvarez: object storage uses customer-managed keys for BYOK; we'll cover re-encryption on restore and key rotations.
[24:15] Maya Chen: circling back to sub-processors — you'll get the list and a diagram from me.
[24:25] Tom Reynolds: do you support data residency tags for specific routes or APIs? e.g., route patient-PII to EU-only route while allowing other anonymized workloads globally.
[24:40] Diego Alvarez: yes, we support per-route policies and tagging; routing can be policy-driven by customer-defined metadata.
[25:05] Sara Patel: ok, good. what about logs retention for audit purposes vs GDPR right to be forgotten?
[25:15] Diego Alvarez: retention policies are configurable; we provide redaction and pseudonymization tools and can segregate audit logs from raw data so deletion requests don't remove audit trail needed for compliance.
[25:40] Tom Reynolds: curious about performance when using HSM-backed BYOK — any throughput impacts?
[25:50] Diego Alvarez: HSM ops are used only at key unwrap/wrap events, not per-token crypto, so throughput impact is minimal; there is slight latency during initial key ops. we'll share numbers.
[26:10] Sara Patel: will you provide certificates for hosted endpoints? mutual TLS?
[26:20] Diego Alvarez: we support mTLS for private endpoints and client cert auth for certain enterprise setups. hosted public APIs use standard TLS with token auth.
[26:45] Aisha Khan: sample legal clause request: include a clause that sub-processors will abide by EU data residency for Medivault data — is that doable?
[26:55] Maya Chen: we'll review with legal; often we can add specific residency commitments in addenda for Dedicated/Private.
[27:20] Tom Reynolds: next step from technical side: Diego to give network diagram and KMS configs; can he also include steps to verify region tap?
[27:30] Diego Alvarez: yes, include routing trace, headers to look for, and how to validate logs.
[27:50] Sara Patel: one more on backup: are backups geo-redundant by default? can we disable cross-region replication?
[28:00] Diego Alvarez: by default hosted may geo-replicate for durability; Dedicated/Private you can disable cross-region replication.
[28:25] Maya Chen: quick summary so far — we'll send SOC2/ISO, sub-processor list, KMS BYOK guide, network diagram, and a pilot proposal.
[28:40] Aisha Khan: please include breach notification timelines and contact points in the docs.
[28:50] Maya Chen: will do.
[29:10] Tom Reynolds: from ops, we'll want an integration checklist for our cloud team.
[29:20] Diego Alvarez: we'll deliver a checklist and sample IaC snippets for VPC endpoints and roles.
[29:45] Sara Patel: any outstanding limitations like telemetry we can't disable?
[29:55] Diego Alvarez: generally we can disable most telemetry flows; there are limited runtime metrics needed for SLA enforcement, but those can be minimized and kept in-region.
[30:20] Maya Chen: switching to procurement questions — Aisha, anything on contracting?
[30:30] Aisha Khan: timeline for legal review depends on DPA complexity; we may need to negotiate residency SLA and sub-processor clauses. please send everything early.
[30:50] Maya Chen: yea we'll prioritize legal pack.
[31:05] Tom Reynolds: runbook question: if we need forensics, can you hand over logs in a forensically sound way (signed, tamper-evident)?
[31:20] Diego Alvarez: logs can be exported with integrity checks and checksums; we'll provide recommended format and retention.
[31:45] Sara Patel: do you provide SOC 2 control mappings to our control set?
[31:55] Maya Chen: yes, we can provide a mapping matrix to common frameworks (ISO/SOC/GDPR). Diego will attach the mapping.
[32:15] Aisha Khan: any cross-border subprocessors in India or US for devops?
[32:25] Maya Chen: some support functions are global; we will provide details and mitigation options (restrict access, JIT, MFA).
[32:40] Tom Reynolds: run a quick hypothetical: if EU region loses capacity and you failover to US, what are the steps to avoid spilling data?
[32:55] Diego Alvarez: we can set policy to fail closed and queue requests, or fail to a secondary EU standby region; default failover to US is opt-in and documented.
[33:20] Sara Patel: curious about key escrow in BYOK scenarios — do you ever hold backups of keys?
[33:30] Diego Alvarez: no, we do not hold private key material for BYOK; we maintain references and grants only. backups controlled by customer KMS.
[33:50] Maya Chen: any further questions from Medivault?
[33:58] Tom Reynolds: stage-wise: once we get docs, we'll run legal review, then tech pilot, then procurement.
[34:15] Sara Patel: timeline ok. please include cost delta between hosted-eu and dedicated-eu for budgeting.
[34:25] Maya Chen: will include a cost estimate and token-level cost comparison.
[34:45] Aisha Khan: please also share sample contract addenda language.
[34:55] Maya Chen: yes.
[35:10] Diego Alvarez: small note — from an engineering perspective, we can instrument a small demo to show end-to-end routing and logs in EU. it takes a couple days to stand up.
[35:30] Tom Reynolds: that's helpful.
[35:50] Sara Patel: any compliance certs beyond SOC2/ISO that matter for healthcare? HITRUST?
[36:00] Maya Chen: we don't currently hold HITRUST but can discuss compensating controls and partnerships; we'll note this.
[36:25] Aisha Khan: if HITRUST becomes a blocker we may need additional controls.
[36:35] Maya Chen: understood.
[36:55] Diego Alvarez: on sub-processors list — we'll flag any that involve cross-border and provide mitigations.
[37:10] Tom Reynolds: for pilot, we'll want a short window of logs retention to validate deletion flows.
[37:20] Diego Alvarez: can do — retention configurable per pilot.
[37:40] Sara Patel: okay, that's mostly it. can you confirm contact points for escalation?
[37:50] Maya Chen: escalation: Maya (AE), Diego (SE), and our security lead (we'll share name) and a 24/7 support channel for enterprise customers.
[38:10] Aisha Khan: will you be sharing a redlineable DPA and sub-processor SLA?
[38:20] Maya Chen: yes.
[38:40] Diego Alvarez: one more technical caveat — some models use token-level analytics to improve quality; for PHI customers we can opt out.
[38:55] Tom Reynolds: good.
[39:10] Sara Patel: let's recap and finalize next steps.
[39:20] Maya Chen: recap: 1) share SOC2/ISO and pentest summary, 2) sub-processor list and data flow diagram, 3) KMS BYOK guide and sample config, 4) network diagram and pilot runbook, 5) cost delta and pilot quote.
[39:50] Tom Reynolds: we'll review docs and get legal to Aisha.
[40:05] Aisha Khan: plan to review within the week.
[40:20] Maya Chen: great — action items and owners on the follow-up email. thanks everyone.
[40:35] Sara Patel: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[40:40] Tom Reynolds: thanks all.
[40:45] Aisha Khan: bye.
[40:50] Maya Chen: end call.
meeting_header: Date: 2026-12-01T15:00:00Z | Duration: 58 mins | Attendees: Maya Chen, Diego Alvarez, Sara Patel, Tom Reynolds, Aisha Khan
notes: Customer requires EU-only processing for PHI and strong contractual guarantees
Recommended Dedicated or Private deployment for strict residency control
BYOK and HSM supported; Redwood to provide KMS integration docs
Audit logs exportable to customer-owned EU logging endpoints
Pilot plan: Dedicated EU env with BYOK, audit log verification, and fault injection
